Marissa / team —

Draft capacity plan below (high-level). I’ll prepare a short PDF with numbers (attached) and we can review on Tue.

Summary recommendation:
- Baseline reserved: 2 x A100-80GB equiv (dedicated instances in Acme VPC) — supports ~55-70 concurrent on typical chat traffic with 95th latency ~200-260ms at 100 token avg.
- Autoscaling policy: add +1 GPU at sustained queue depth > 30 requests for 60s, add +2 GPUs when queue depth > 60 requests for 30s.
- Burst capacity: pre-warm 2 additional GPUs for demo windows (Croned start 2 mins before expected demo). If unknown, enable conservative burst-on-demand with warm-up ~90s (cold-start for large models ~60-120s depending on kernel warmup).
- Cost/cap estimate for 3-week POC: baseline reserved + average autoscale usage expected to incur ~35% uplift vs baseline hour cost. See attached estimate.

Notes and mitigations:
- We can reduce tail latency by: increased batching thresholds for background requests, KV prefix caching for repeated context, and enabling quantization profile tuned for 256-token runs. Expect ~10-20% latency improvement with caching.
- For spike protection: implement queue-based shedding and graceful degradation to a smaller model variant if latency or queue exceeds hard limits (we'll propose fallback policy during canary).
- Required access: AWS role for Private control plane, KMS key ARN, and VPC peering details.

Attachments: redwood-poc-capacity-estimate.pdf (contains cost and concurrency tables)

Let me know if you want me on the kickoff with Acme on Feb 24 or Mar 1.

—Dylan
